destination.name: Madang
destination.tagline: A small harbour town on Papua New Guinea's north coast, used as a base for diving and island trips.
destination.description: Madang is the capital of Madang Province, a town of almost 30,000 people on the north coast of Papua New Guinea. People come for scuba diving in the nearby waters and for a small, relatively safe town to walk around by day. Japan captured it in 1942 and Australian forces retook it on 24 April 1944, after fighting that virtually destroyed it; it was then rebuilt. The airport closes at 5 PM to avoid collisions with flying foxes at dusk.
whyVisit: Hike to the crater on Karkar Island

goodToKnow.title: Pre-arrange evening drivers
goodToKnow.detail: There are no taxis, it is almost impossible to get around town after 6 PM, and walking after dark is not advisable. For dinner anywhere other than your hotel, book a driver in advance; most evenings will be at your hotel or resort.

goodToKnow.title: Market for food, shops for crafts
goodToKnow.detail: The central market is open every day except Sunday and sells mostly fruit and vegetables. The craft shops at Madang Resort and Madang Lodge are probably the best places in town to buy crafts. Minivan buses to nearby towns leave from the central bus station near the market.

goodToKnow.title: Crocodiles and malaria
goodToKnow.detail: Saltwater crocodiles are common in Papua New Guinea's coastal waters and rivers, and the advice is to avoid swimming except in hotel pools or at higher elevations; ask locally before using the small swimming spots along Madang's shoreline. Malaria is also a hazard, so ask a doctor about prevention before you travel.
